title: The Historical Jesus
description:
S01 E03 — Scholars Look at the Gospels
The work of German writer D. F. Strauss argues that the Gospels are best understood as containing history-like stories that intend to convey truth but do not occur as they are narrated, which is why most scholars find his approach illuminating.

title: The Historical Jesus
description:
S01 E04 — Fact and Fiction in the Gospels
Scholars question the historical accuracy of some gospel accounts not out of hostility toward Christianity, but because of historical evidence; what this evidence is; how historians assess it.

title: Archaeology: An Introduction to the World's Greatest Sites
description:
S01 E01 — The Origins of Modern Archaeology
What archeologists actually do; the nature and scope of their work; misconceptions about the field; tracing the history of archeology, from its beginnings with the ancient Babylonian king Nabonidus to archeological luminaries of the 20th century.

title: Archaeology: An Introduction to the World's Greatest Sites
description:
S01 E02 — Excavating Pompeii and Herculaneum
Traveling to the sites of Pompeii and Herculaneum, which are destroyed by the 79 A.D. eruption of Mount Vesuvius; the history of their excavation; the preservation of buildings, objects and human remains; discovering details of ancient Roman life.

title: Archaeology: An Introduction to the World's Greatest Sites
description:
S01 E03 — Schliemann and His Successors at Troy
Following the exploits of Heinrich Schliemann as he looks for Homer's Troy; learning about his dig through nine stratified cities; the finds; the debates over which city is Troy; tracing subsequent work at the site; examining the conclusions.

title: Archaeology: An Introduction to the World's Greatest Sites
description:
S01 E04 — Early Archaeology in Mesopotamia
The history of finds in Mesopotamia; the 19th-century unearthing of the Assyrian palaces at Nimrud and Nineveh, with their libraries of cuneiform texts; contemplating the 20th-century discovery of the treasures of the "Death Pits of Ur".

title: War in the Modern World
description:
S01 E01 — Afghanistan and the Nature of Modern War
In the course's inaugural episode, begin to explore the transformation of violent conflicts between major world powers by delving into a particularly recent example: America's 20-year war in Afghanistan.

title: War in the Modern World
description:
S01 E02 — Nightmare Scenarios of Modern War
The factors that explain why wars between great powers look different nowadays, and explore what future conflicts could look like between the United States and two of its major adversaries.

title: War in the Modern World
description:
S01 E03 — The Tools of Modern Warfare
How five contemporary technologies-the Kalashnikov assault rifle, improvised explosive devices, guided missiles, drones, and cyber warfare-redefined the rules of battle and leveled the playing field between world powers and insurgent groups.

title: War in the Modern World
description:
S01 E04 — From World War to Cold War
The series of events that followed World War II from the allied occupation of Germany to the Greek Civil War; how the Soviet Union contended with insurgencies and the beginnings of conflict between the United States and the USSR.

title: War in the Modern World
description:
S01 E05 — Europe's Exit from Colonial Asia
The future of occupied Asia becomes murky after 1945; few people want to see colonial occupiers reassert their influence; zeroing in on conflicts in Indonesia, the Philippines and India to see how geopolitics in the region transform after the war.

title: War in the Modern World
description:
S01 E06 — China's Civil War
As war rages on across the globe, China has to contend with civil war; exploring the war from its colonial roots to the establishment of the People's Republic of China; how the U.S.S.R. and the United States get involved in the conflict.

title: War in the Modern World
description:
S01 E07 — The Unfinished Korean War
Why America fights a war in Korea; how the U.S.S.R. engages in the conflict; whether the United States could wage a limited war on the peninsula as it intends to; what to make of a war that ends not in peace, but in an armistice.

title: War in the Modern World
description:
S01 E08 — Britain's Exit from Palestine, Malaya, and Kenya
After World War II, organized rebellions explode within the British Empire; investigating the conflicts that shake postwar Palestine, Kenya and Malaya; British counterinsurgency tactics; what these confrontations reveal about war and colonialism.

title: The Great Trials of World History and the Lessons They Teach Us
description:
S01 E01 — The Trial of Socrates
Surveying some of history's greatest trials with a visit to ancient Athens; in 399 B.C., Socrates undergoes his trial for corrupting Athenians and disrespecting their gods; In the process, he lectures his jurors on the duty of seeking the truth.

title: The Great Trials of World History and the Lessons They Teach Us
description:
S01 E02 — The Trial of Gaius Verres
To save the Roman Republic, Cicero charges Gaius Verres, a provincial governor, with crimes against the people; Cicero's Actio Secunda aims to educate the Roman public about the corruption and rot in its political system.

title: The Great Trials of World History and the Lessons They Teach Us
description:
S01 E03 — Three Medieval Trials
Studying three strange trials from the Middle Ages; the first involves a dead pope put on trial; the second involves an accused adulterer's walk over red-hot ploughshares. The third involves a battle whose victor is vindicated as a matter of law.

title: The Great Trials of World History and the Lessons They Teach Us
description:
S01 E04 — The Trial of Sir Thomas More
Traveling back to Westminster Hall on July 1, 1535, when Sir Thomas Moore stands on trial for his refusal to acknowledge King Henry VIII as head of the Church of England; one of England's most revered men ends up on the chopping block.

title: The Great Trials of World History and the Lessons They Teach Us
description:
S01 E05 — The Trial of Giordano Bruno
Giordano Bruno's ideas on natural philosophy are dangerous to 16th-century thought; his execution represents a failure of the Roman Inquisition to perform its mission to admonish, not punish; the impact of this trial on another heresy case.

title: The Great Trials of World History and the Lessons They Teach Us
description:
S01 E06 — The Salem Witchcraft Trials
According to Professor Linder, the Salem witchcraft trials illustrate the danger of drawing conclusions ahead of evidence; gaining a greater understanding of the legal basis for a travesty that accuses hundreds of people of practicing witchcraft.

title: The Great Trials of World History and the Lessons They Teach Us
description:
S01 E07 — The Boston Massacre Trials
A harbinger of the American Revolution, the Boston Massacre trials reflect the heated partisanship of the times; the young attorney John Adams pays a price for his decision to represent the accused British soldiers and their captain.

title: The Great Trials of World History and the Lessons They Teach Us
description:
S01 E08 — The Aaron Burr Conspiracy Trial
Learning whether politics and justice can be kept separate in great trials; considering the conspiracy trial of Aaron Burr presided over by Chief Justice John Marshall; no one in the United States, even the president, is above the law.

title: The American West: History, Myth, and Legacy
description:
S01 E01 — Westward the Course of Empire
Some of the ways people think about the American West; how this vast, fascinating region comes into being; how it is shaped by centuries of myth-making; what about westward expansion fascinates every generation of Americans.

title: The American West: History, Myth, and Legacy
description:
S01 E02 — The West in the Colonial Era
Understanding the mark left on the American West by its earliest colonists; the Spaniards, who introduce horses; the French, who develop a complex trade system; the English, who have little interest in colonizing the west of the Appalachians.

title: The Real History of Pirates
description:
S01 E01 — What is a Pirate?
Exploring the reasons piracy endures from ancient times until today; why it is so difficult to both define and eradicate; how one can understand the rule of law and the rights of nations and individuals on the high seas and in borderless realms.

title: The Real History of Pirates
description:
S01 E02 — Pirate Facts and Fictions
Examining popular pirate legends; discovering which aspects include some truth and which contain none at all; pirate literature can teach a lot about the Jolly Roger, gold-filled treasure chests, the pirate Edward Thatch and more.

title: The Vietnam War
description:
S01 E01 — America Enters the War
U.S. Marines arrive in June 1965 to protect a U.S. air base; the North Vietnamese Army and the southern Viet Cong guerrillas launch attacks.

title: The Vietnam War
description:
S01 E02 — French Indochina and the Viet Minh
Surveying the economic exploitation and repression that defines Vietnam in the 19th and early 20th centuries.

title: The American Civil War
description:
S01 E01 — Prelude to War
Learning about the sectional controversies and clashes that ultimately set the stage for secession and war.

title: The American Civil War
description:
S01 E02 — The Election of 1860
The presidential canvass of 1860 is the most important in U.S. history; it results in Abraham Lincoln's election as the first Republican to occupy the White House and brings sectional tensions to a head.

title: American Military History: From Colonials to Counterinsurgents
description:
S01 E01 — America: Forged in War
Exploring The French and Indian War of the mid-1700s, which is one of the formative conflicts in American military history; focusing on the experiences of Lt. Col. George Washington, a young colonial officer fighting for the British.

title: American Military History: From Colonials to Counterinsurgents
description:
S01 E02 — George Washington Takes Command
When the colonies begin their struggle for independence, they choose George Washington to lead the army; Washington's defense of Boston; his defeat trying to hold New York City; contrasting British and American objectives in the Revolutionary War.

title: Warriors, Queens, and Intellectuals: 36 Great Women Before 1400
description:
S01 E01 — Julia Disobeys Emperor Augustus
The experiences of Julia, the daughter of Caesar Augustus; a window into the way many pre-modern societies sought to control morality; Julia's life of thwarted potential; understanding what women had to overcome to make a mark on history.

title: Warriors, Queens, and Intellectuals: 36 Great Women Before 1400
description:
S01 E02 — Herodias Has John the Baptist Beheaded
The portrayal of the John the Baptist's death as the whim of the young femme fatale Salome; why the truth is much more complicated; the story of Salome's mother, Herodias; how Herodias's hunger for power and recognition left her exiled and forgotten.

title: Unsung Heroes of World War II: Europe
description:
S01 E01 — Andrée de Jongh and the Resistance
When the Germans begin their rapid invasions across Europe, many ordinary citizens are stunned; Dedee de Jongh, a 23-year-old nurse, builds an escape line through Belgium and France to rescue stranded British airmen; her courage and ingenuity.

title: Unsung Heroes of World War II: Europe
description:
S01 E02 — The Tory Rebels Who Helped Save England
In hindsight, it may appear inevitable that Winston Churchill takes command; at the time, it seems unthinkable that Neville Chamberlain steps down; how a few brave politicians orchestrate one of the most striking political transitions in history.

title: The Celtic World
description:
S01 E01 — Who Are the Celts?
Examining and clarifying common preconceptions about Celtic identity; painting the initial brushstrokes on the canvas of a European culture most widely perceived as Scottish and Irish while promising much more.

title: The Celtic World
description:
S01 E02 — The Celts and the Classical World
Studying the earliest written records of the Celts from Italy, Greece and Spain, dating as far back as the sixth century B.C.; scholarly theories about the Celts' migration throughout Europe; the foundation of humanity's understanding of the Celts.

title: The Celtic World
description:
S01 E03 — Celtic Art and Artifacts
How archeological studies of Celtic artifacts have woven a rich tapestry of their millennia-old society; learning about war trumpets, gold necklaces and other recovered objects from around Europe; building an image of this ever-adapting culture.

title: The Celtic World
description:
S01 E04 — Celtic Languages in the Ancient World
The discovery of Celtic inscriptions on Spain's western coast; the possibility of a common language along maritime trade routes; revolutionizing studies of Celtic origins and migration; the long-standing theory of Central European Celtic origins.

title: The Celtic World
description:
S01 E05 — Caesar and the Gauls
How several centuries of combat against Celtic-controlled Gaul made northern Italy and southern France a dangerous place for the Romans; Julius Caesar's wars against the Gauls; famous figures of world history and their encounters with the Gauls.

title: The Celtic World
description:
S01 E06 — Celtic Religion and the Druids
Celtic religious beliefs in divination, reincarnation and human sacrifice; discovering the ancient religious figures known as druids, who served as holy men, soothsayers, and even lawyers; an insight into the Celtic version of the sacred.

title: The Celtic World
description:
S01 E07 — Celtic Britain and Roman Britain
The theory of trade-based migration to explain the arrival of the Celts' influence in Britain before the arrival of the Romans; the struggle between the Celts and the Romans over Britain; untangling a web of history on the island.

title: The Celtic World
description:
S01 E08 — Celts and Picts in Scotland
Life in Scotland during the time of a Romanized southern Britain; the warring tribes of Picts that ruled North Britain; highlights that include the ancient Pictish tongue and the truth about William "Braveheart" Wallace.

title: The United States and the Middle East: 1914 to 9/11
description:
S01 E01 — A Meeting of Two Worlds
Introducing the themes of increasing American power; indigenous political aspirations; conflicting interests and goals; growing mutual antagonism; setting the stage for World War I.

title: The United States and the Middle East: 1914 to 9/11
description:
S01 E02 — Wilson & the Breakup of the Ottoman Empire
An examination of wartime and postwar American policy; showing how Wilson's commitment to an ethnocentrically defined view of national self-determination drives his efforts to shape the postwar settlement in the Middle East.

title: The United States and the Middle East: 1914 to 9/11
description:
S01 E03 — The Interwar Period
American interest in the Middle East between the wars; revealing one's focus shifting in the 1930s to American interest in Saudi Arabian oil; the increasing activism of American Zionism in response to Hitler's persecution of German Jews.

title: The United States and the Middle East: 1914 to 9/11
description:
S01 E04 — U.S. & the Middle East During World War II
United States' entry into World War II alters Americans' conception of the Middle East; the Middle East's geopolitical orientation is now seen as vital to American security.

title: Creation Stories of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E01 — Creation Stories and Why They Matter
Considering the nature of creation stories.

title: Creation Stories of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E02 — Reading Metaphor in Creation Stories
Metaphor and symbol are integral to creation stories, as they form a crucial part of the language of myth.

title: Creation Stories of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E03 — Mesopotamian Creation: Enuma elish
Enuma Elish, also called the Seven Tablets of Creation, is a masterpiece of Mesopotamian literature.

title: Creation Stories of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E04 — The Mesopotamian Flood: The Atrahasis Epic
Examining key Mesopotamian texts referencing a catastrophic flood which decimates humanity.

title: Turning Points in Middle Eastern History
description:
S01 E01 — Muslim Empires: Land, Language, Religion
The geographical region known as Greater Middle East; the range of nations and cultures that define it; historical turning points to witness, encompassing conquests, political alliances and Islam's rise; social, intellectual and economic reforms.

title: Turning Points in Middle Eastern History
description:
S01 E02 — Muhammad and the Dawn of Islam - 622
Islam's rise is a major turning point; tracing key phases in the life of Muhammad (PBUH); the founding of the faith through his years of opposition; his establishment of Islam as a religious and political entity; the global impact of these events.

title: Turning Points in Middle Eastern History
description:
S01 E03 — Arab Invasion of North Africa - 639
The seventh-century Arab invasion of North Africa brings profound change to the entire region; the Arab armies of the newly created Islamic empire try to conquer the territories of Egypt and others; the lasting Arabization and Islamization.

title: Turning Points in Middle Eastern History
description:
S01 E04 — Umayyad Caliphate in Damascus - 661
The establishment of the Umayyad Caliphate's capital in Damascus is a key event in early Muslim history; the Umayyads' achievements; locating the empire's capital away from the Arabian Peninsula; the shift from an Islamic empire to imperial power.

title: Great Board Games of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E01 — Bearing Off: The Story of Backgammon
During the Third Crusade, the European soldiers spend the winter playing the ancient game of Tables, which would evolve into backgammon by the 20th century.

title: Great Board Games of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E02 — Senet: Egypt's Game of the Afterlife
Unearthed artifacts from King Tutankhamun's tomb include Senet boards. Historians study the hieroglyphs and investigate the abrupt disappearance of this ancient Egyptian game.

title: Great Board Games of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E03 — Chess: The Evolution of a Strategy Icon
Developed during the Guptas' rule in India, Chaturanga is a strategy game resembling chess. It gradually wended its way westward to become what it is in the present.

title: Great Board Games of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E04 — Chess's Eastern Cousins: Shogi and Xiangqi
The East Asian games of Xiangqi and Shogi are potentially connected to Chaturanga and chess, but a lack of documentation makes it difficult to ascertain anything.

title: Investigating American Presidents
description:
S01 E01 — American Presidents and the Rule of Law
Exploring the roots of the presidency and presidential power as outlined in the Constitution; the advantages and disadvantages a president has during an investigation; why presidential investigations are essential knowledge for any American citizen.

title: Investigating American Presidents
description:
S01 E02 — Presidential Investigations through History
Presidential crises and abuses of power; early executive scandals and their significant long-term effects; how people are still dealing with the fallout of famous investigations; the controversies of Ulysses S. Grant and Warren G. Harding.

title: Investigating American Presidents
description:
S01 E03 — Separation of Powers and the Presidency
Legislative and judicial oversight of the presidency as a permanent part of the American government; limiting and restraining the possibility of executive abuse; how a system of checks and balances came to exist; the case of Marbury v. Madison.
